### 14.1 Auto-memory hooks (StrongHold "kicks on" automatically)

The MCP makes the tools *available*; these optional hooks make Claude Code *use* memory
on its own — no need to remember to call the tools. The helper **`service/sh-memory.mjs`**
talks to the same backend over HTTP (hooks can't call MCP tools) and reads the same
`~/.stronghold/mcp.json` token, so **it writes to your own tenant automatically** — each
colleague's notes stay isolated to their tenant (and, if that tenant has a provisioned
filespace, ride mem-sync into it).

What it does:
- **SessionStart** → recalls notes relevant to the current project, injects them as context.
- **SessionEnd** → a *detached* worker distills up to 5 durable takeaways via your **local**
  model tier and stores them. Non-blocking; skips trivial sessions.

Both are **fail-safe**: no token / backend down / any error → exit 0 with no output, so a
hook never blocks or breaks a session. All notes go to one long-lived per-tenant
`claude-code-notes` agent (used for both recall and remember).

Setup:
```bash
# 1. Install the helper (it's standalone Node; needs your ~/.stronghold/mcp.json token).
mkdir -p ~/.stronghold && cp service/sh-memory.mjs ~/.stronghold/sh-memory.mjs

# 2. Add two hooks to your GLOBAL settings (~/.claude/settings.json), under "hooks".
title: StrongHold — Developer Quickstart

text:
#    Replace the node path with `which node` on your machine.
```
```jsonc
"SessionStart": [
  { "hooks": [
    { "type": "command",
      "command": "/path/to/node ~/.stronghold/sh-memory.mjs session-start",
      "timeout": 8000, "statusMessage": "Loading StrongHold memory…" } ] }
],
"SessionEnd": [
  { "hooks": [
    { "type": "command",
      "command": "/path/to/node ~/.stronghold/sh-memory.mjs remember",
      "timeout": 8000, "statusMessage": "Saving session takeaways to StrongHold…" } ] }
]
```
Merge into existing `SessionStart`/`SessionEnd` arrays rather than replacing them. Hooks
take effect on the next session. To disable, delete the two entries (or open `/hooks`).
Per-prompt recall is intentionally omitted (latency/noise); `sh-memory.mjs recall` exists
if you want to wire a `UserPromptSubmit` hook yourself.

## 15. Token & usage metering

Every model call's token usage is captured from the provider and normalized to
`{input, output, total}`, so you can see exactly how many tokens each model / provider / tool
burned — local (free/sovereign) vs cloud (paid) spend, with no external dashboard.

**Per call.** `chat` / `act` / `fanout` responses now carry a `usage` block. For `act` and
`fanout` it is **summed** across every model call in the agentic loop / across all sub-agents:

```jsonc
// POST /agents/{id}/chat
{
  "text": "Launch is Sept 9.",
  "provider": "ollama",
  "model": "qwen2.5-coder:32b",
  "usage": { "input": 56, "output": 5, "total": 61 }
}
```

**Cumulative (process-wide).** The internal service `GET /healthz` reports `usageTotals` since
process start, broken down by provider and by model:

```jsonc
// GET /healthz  (internal service)
"usageTotals": {
  "totals":     { "input": 1234, "output": 890, "total": 2124, "calls": 7 },
  "byProvider": { "ollama": { "input": 600, "output": 61, "total": 661, "calls": 4 } },
  "byModel":    { "deepseek-r1:32b": { "input": 44, "output": 557, "total": 601, "calls": 1 } }
}
```

**Per session (MCP).** From Claude Code, call **`stronghold_usage`** for this session's running
totals plus a per-tool breakdown — it's client-side bookkeeping, no backend round-trip.

## 16. Routing to more models & backends

StrongHold is no longer pinned to one local model + cloud. Beyond the `tier` knob (§9), pass an
explicit `model` to route by **what the model is** — an explicit `model` always wins over tier
ordering:

| `model` form | Routes to | Example |
|---|---|---|
| bare model name | the **Ollama pool** (a host that actually has it) | `"deepseek-r1:32b"` |
| `"<backend>/<model>"` | a registered OpenAI-compatible backend (below) | `"webui/llama3.1:70b"` |
| `vendor/model` OpenRouter slug | OpenRouter (see §9) | `"google/gemini-2.0-flash"` |

Extra models already loaded on the cluster Ollamas (`deepseek-r1:32b`, `qwen2.5:32b`,
`llama3.1:70b`, …) are reachable + metered **by name with zero config** — just name them.

You can also map a bare `tier` to a specific cluster model with **tier→model aliases** in

text:
# StrongHold — Executive Brief

*StrongHold is our Harness as a Service (HaaS).*

**One line:** A private AI-agent platform that runs entirely on hardware we already
own — giving us the capabilities of a commercial cloud "AI agent service" without
sending our data, our code, or our customers' information to a third party.

---

## The idea

Every modern AI product is built on a *harness* — the software around an AI model that
lets it actually do work: remember things, use tools, run code, and take multi-step
actions. Today most companies rent that harness from the big AI labs and run it inside
the labs' cloud, paying per use and trusting an outside vendor with their data.

StrongHold is not merely our own copy of that harness — it is a **metaharness**: a layer
that sits *above* the AI vendors and treats each one (our own on-premise model, Claude,
GPT, Gemini, and others) as an interchangeable part. The big labs build a harness *for
their model*, with their model at the center — by design, to keep you on it. StrongHold
puts the **orchestration** at the center and demotes every model to a swappable component
we choose per task. Same capabilities — **owned end to end, data kept local, and beholden
to no single vendor.**

## Why it matters

| | Rented cloud harness | StrongHold |
|---|---|---|
| **Data** | Sent to a vendor's cloud | Stays on our hardware by default |
| **Cost** | Metered per use, indefinitely | Fixed hardware we already own; cloud models optional |
| **Lock-in** | Tied to one vendor's models | Any model — our own, Claude, or others — swappable |
| **Control** | Vendor sets the rules | We own the stack, the memory, and the data |
title: StrongHold — Executive Brief

text:
## Two things only StrongHold has

Most of what StrongHold does, a rented cloud harness can also do. Two things it
**structurally cannot**, and they are the moat:

1. **It's a metaharness — it orchestrates the orchestrators.** A rented harness can run
   *its own* model and *its own* tools. StrongHold runs *any* model and absorbs *entire
   other AI systems* as interchangeable parts behind one interface, choosing the cheapest
   model that's good enough for each task and falling over to another vendor mid-job if
   one fails. The big labs can't copy this — their business depends on their model being
   the center, not a swappable part. We are the layer that makes *their* product one of
   *our* backends.

2. **One shared source of truth across every agent, everywhere — on LucidLink.** This is
   the part we have badly undersold. LucidLink is a single, global, streaming filesystem:
   every agent — on either Spark, on the Mac, at the Florida or California sites — reads
   and writes the **same** files, instantly, with no copying and no "which version is
   right?" Our agents are short-lived by design; the *truth* can't live inside any one of
   them. On LucidLink it lives in one durable, versioned, shared place that no single
   agent owns and that outlives all of them. That gives us something a rented memory
   store fundamentally isn't: **one canonical memory for the whole fleet**, that we own,
   that streams on demand (so no machine has to hold the whole corpus), and that we never
   pay a vendor to replicate or query. The metaharness is the brain; **LucidLink is the
   shared, sovereign memory all the brains agree on.**
title: StrongHold — Executive Brief

text:
## The economics

The headline isn't "it's cheaper." It's that StrongHold **inverts the cost curve**:

- **We already paid for the hardware (capex is sunk); every extra agent run is then
  essentially free** — the marginal cost of a local request is electricity, not a
  per-token fee. A rented harness is pure ongoing cost that scales *up* with success: the
  more value you get from it, the more you pay, forever.
- **The cost gap is widest exactly where the value is highest.** A one-shot chat is cheap
  to rent. An *agent* that reasons over many steps and fans out to sub-agents makes dozens
  of model calls per task — and a rented harness meters every one. Those agentic
  workloads, the valuable ones, are where renting hurts most and where owning the GPUs
  flips the math.
- **Cloud is opt-in and surgical.** The default path is our free on-premise model. We pay
  premium frontier prices *only* on the specific requests that ask for "best." So we get a
  blended cost — free for the routine 90%, premium for the 10% that earns it — instead of
  paying a premium price for 100% of calls.
- **The whole memory layer is free.** Embeddings, search, and recall run on-device. On a
  rented stack each of those is separately metered (per-embedding, per-vector stored,
  per-query). With LucidLink + our own object storage, one canonical copy streams to every
  agent — we don't pay to duplicate, sync, or query memory across machines or sites.
- **No lock-in means pricing power.** Because models are swappable, no vendor can raise
  prices on us without us routing around them. The metaharness is itself a cost-control
  engine: it spends frontier dollars only where they pay for themselves.
- **It resells with real margin.** Because the marginal cost of serving a tenant is near
  zero, a product built *on* StrongHold has gross margins limited only by hardware we've
  already bought. A competitor reselling a rented harness has the vendor's per-token fee as
  a permanent floor under their costs.
title: StrongHold — Executive Brief

text:
## What it runs on

StrongHold runs on two NVIDIA DGX Spark supercomputers that we already own. The
everyday AI work is handled by our own on-premise model at zero per-use cost. By
default, **no data leaves our hardware** — a credible, concrete answer to the question
every customer and partner eventually asks: *"Where does our data go?"*
title: StrongHold — Executive Brief

text:
## What's new

This release moves StrongHold from a working prototype to a resilient, shareable
platform. The headline additions:

- **Double the horsepower from hardware we already own.** StrongHold now uses *both*
  DGX Spark machines together as a single pool, running two AI jobs at the same time —
  one on each — for roughly **2× the throughput** with no new hardware spend. If one
  machine is busy or briefly unavailable, work automatically shifts to the other.

- **The agents can now work over our own files.** StrongHold can securely read the
  team's existing LucidLink files — searching, reading, and reasoning over documents we
  already control. The connection is **read-only** (it cannot change or delete files),
  and the file content stays inside our environment.

- **Hardened for resilience — it heals itself.** Connections and helper services that
  drop are detected and automatically restarted. Every AI request has a time limit, so
  a stuck machine triggers an automatic switch to a backup rather than hanging. If all
  of our local capacity is occupied, StrongHold can **automatically fail over to a
  cloud model** to keep responding — then return to local-first by default. Memory is
  written to disk before anything is reported as "saved," so a restart never loses or
  silently corrupts data.

- **Hardened for security.** Each customer gets their own **usage limits** so no single
  tenant can overwhelm the system. The platform **refuses to start** with a weak or
  missing security key (it "fails closed" instead of running insecurely). Any code the
  agents run executes in a **locked-down sandbox** — no network access, no special
  privileges, strict time and memory limits. And our sensitive credentials are kept
  away from the helper tools: **no third-party component ever receives our API keys.**
  The platform itself now runs **with no special privileges on the host machine** — so
  even a full compromise of the agent process or its sandbox cannot take over the
  underlying computer. The connection to our own files runs over a **single-purpose,
  locked-down key** that can do nothing but read those files.

- **Cost visibility, built in — see every token as it's spent (2026-06-30).** StrongHold
  now meters every AI call and shows exactly how many tokens each model, provider, and
  tool consumed — broken out **live by backend**, so the free, sovereign on-premise work
  and the paid cloud spend are visible side by side, in real time, with no external
  dashboard or third-party billing tool. Cost attribution is now a property of the
  platform itself, not something we reconstruct after the fact.

- **Any model on the cluster, swappable by configuration (2026-06-30).** StrongHold is no
  longer pinned to a single local model plus cloud. It now routes to *any* model running
  on our cluster — including more, larger, or specialized local models — and is wired to
  reach *any* standard ("OpenAI-compatible") inference engine, all selectable by
  configuration with **no code change**. The extra local models are live and metered
  today; the additional outside engines are wired and ready, awaiting only their access
  keys. Combined with the metering above, every backend we add arrives with its
  usage and cost already visible.

- **Shareable with colleagues.** StrongHold is multi-tenant and sits behind a sign-in,
  so colleagues can each be given their own isolated workspace on the same shared
  platform, with their data walled off from everyone else's.
title: StrongHold — Executive Brief

text:
## What it can do today

- **Remembers** — persistent, per-user memory that survives restarts; each user's data
  is isolated from the rest.
- **Converses** — answers questions grounded in that memory.
- **Acts** — autonomous agents that can write and run code in the secure sandbox to
  complete real tasks, not just chat.
- **Connects** — plugs into our own tools and files (including LucidLink) to do useful
  work over data we already own.
- **Chooses the right model** — uses our private on-premise model by default, and can
  escalate to top-tier cloud models on demand, with automatic fallback if one is
  unavailable. The user simply asks for "fast" or "best" and never has to pick a model.
  Behind that simple choice, the pool of models it can reach is now open-ended: any model
  on our cluster and any standard inference engine we wire in, swappable by configuration.
- **Shows what it costs** — every call is metered, so token usage is visible per model,
  provider, and tool in real time, making the free local vs. paid cloud spend plain as
  you work.
title: StrongHold — Executive Brief

text:
## Strategic value

1. **A real moat — the metaharness.** We don't own a model; we own the *layer above the
   models*. That's the durable, defensible asset competitors who only rent the cloud
   can't replicate, because their whole model depends on keeping their model at the center.
2. **One sovereign memory for the whole fleet — LucidLink.** Every agent, on every
   machine and site, shares one canonical, streaming, versioned source of truth that we
   own. This is both a capability no rented memory store offers and a cost advantage (no
   replication, no per-query fees).
3. **Inverted cost curve** — sunk hardware means near-zero marginal cost per agent run;
   paid cloud models are opt-in per request. Costs fall as volume grows, instead of
   rising with it.
4. **Privacy & sovereignty** — a credible answer to "where does our data go?": *nowhere
   it doesn't have to.*
5. **More value from owned assets** — the dual-machine capability roughly doubles
   throughput from the cluster we already paid for, at zero new spend.
6. **No lock-in = pricing power** — we adopt the best (or cheapest-adequate) model from
   any vendor without re-platforming, and route around price hikes.

## Status

- **Live** and serving requests over a secure connection, on our own hardware.
- All major resilience and security improvements above are **done and verified live**.
- As of **2026-06-30**, built-in cost metering (per model, provider, and tool) and routing
  to additional models on the cluster are **live and verified**; the path to outside
  inference engines is wired and awaits only their activation keys.
- **Multi-tenant** — designed to sit behind a customer-facing app (currently wired to a
  Lovable frontend) with per-user isolation. As of 2026-06-30 each tenant's *learned*
  knowledge is also isolated: what one workspace teaches the system stays private to that
  workspace; only explicitly-curated shared knowledge is common. Each tenant's memory also
  lands in its own folder in the shared storage namespace.

text:
## Before a broad external rollout (known next steps)

This is an early but genuinely working platform, and the previously-flagged knowledge-sharing
gap is now closed (learned knowledge is per-tenant). Two items remain before exposing it
*widely* (neither blocks internal use or a pilot): (1) tightening who can sign up and adding
spend caps on the paid AI tiers — the per-model and per-tenant cost visibility those caps
build on is now in place, so this narrows to enforcing limits on top of numbers we already
track; and (2) the strongest form of storage isolation — giving each
customer their **own** encrypted storage space rather than a shared one partitioned by folder —
which we can provision through the workspace gateway we already built.

text:
## 1. What it is

**StrongHold** is a **sovereign, memory-centric AI-agent *metaharness***, served as an API, running
entirely on the owner's own hardware (two NVIDIA DGX Spark supercomputers). A "harness" (per Dan
Cleary's *Harness as a Service*) is everything around a model that lets it do real work: the agent
loop, tool runtime, sandbox, memory, session/auth, and model routing. The labs (Anthropic, OpenAI,
Cursor) sell a *managed* harness in their cloud — a harness built *for their model*, with their
model at the center.

**StrongHold is a metaharness: it orchestrates the orchestrators.** The model, the tool runtime,
the sandbox, the memory backend, and even whole external agent frameworks (ruflo/claude-flow over
MCP) are interchangeable leaves. The orchestration sits *above* them, and every model is a
swappable commodity chosen per request. A harness orchestrates tool calls; a metaharness
orchestrates harnesses. (See §1a.) StrongHold is the same capability set as a rented "AI agent
service" — **owned end-to-end, with data kept local, and beholden to no single vendor**:

- **Sovereign** — runs on DGX Spark hardware; inference goes to a local LLM pool over the cluster
  network; data never leaves your hardware unless a request explicitly opts into a cloud model.
- **Metaharness / model-agnostic** — local model by default; Claude and OpenRouter
  (GPT/Gemini/Llama/…) are opt-in tiers with automatic failover. The model is a leaf, not the
  center.
- **Memory-centric, with a fleet-wide source of truth** — persistent, per-tenant, branchable
  memory is the centerpiece; LucidLink provides one shared, sovereign source of truth across every
  agent and site (see §4.5).
- **Multi-tenant** — per-user isolation via JWT, designed to back a Lovable (or any) frontend.

Repo root on host: `/home/markt/agenticow-ruflo-memory`. Private GitHub repo
`markt-heximal/StrongHold`. Category: **Harness as a Service (HaaS)** — specifically, a *metaharness*.

text:
## 1a. The metaharness thesis (positioning)

The frontier model is hard to replicate; **the harness around it is not** — it is orchestration
plumbing. The labs bundle the two and price the bundle as if the harness were the scarce part. It
isn't. StrongHold's thesis is to **own the plumbing and rent the model à la carte**, only on the
calls that genuinely need a frontier brain.

| | Rented harness (the labs) | StrongHold (metaharness) |
|---|---|---|
| Center of gravity | *Their* model | *Your* orchestration; models are leaves |
| Models available | One vendor's | Local + Claude + OpenRouter (any slug), swapped per task, with mid-task failover |
| Other agent frameworks | N/A | Absorbed as just-another-toolset via MCP (ruflo's 305 tools curated to 8) |
| Code execution | Their black-box interpreter | Your sovereign rootless-Docker sandbox (caps/network/limits you set) |
| Source of truth | Their memory store | LucidLink — one global filesystem you own (§4.5) |
| Lock-in | By design | Structurally none — every model is interchangeable |

This is a difference the labs **cannot** copy without abandoning their business model: their
economics depend on their model being the center, whereas a metaharness demotes every model to a
commodity. StrongHold is the layer that makes *their* product one of *our* backends.

The two things that make StrongHold categorically different (not just a cheaper clone) are this
**metaharness** structure and the **LucidLink single source of truth** in §4.5. Read them as the
headline; everything else is implementation.

## 4. Memory
title: StrongHold — System Documentation

text:
### 4.1 Per-user copy-on-write memory (the core)
- Built on **agenticow** — copy-on-write vector branching ("Git for agent memory"). A shared
  **base** plus cheap per-agent **branches**. Each agent has private memory over the shared base;
  on recall, the agent's private memories union with the base (child wins on id collision).
- **Embeddings are local**: `Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` (384-dim) — no network, no token cost, works
  offline. Memory is model-independent.
- **graduate-on-terminate (per-tenant, 2026-06-30)**: deleting an agent promotes its vetted
  memories into its **tenant's** base scope `tbase:<tenant>` (ids preserved), then releases the
  branch. Every one of that tenant's agents inherits `tbase:<tenant>` at spawn, and
  `/memory/search` recalls over a per-tenant base — so a tenant's graduated learnings reach only
  that tenant's future agents, never across tenants. The **global** agenticow base is reserved for
  explicitly-curated shared infra (`addKnowledge`) and is no longer fed by auto-graduation.
  (Untagged/legacy agents fall back to the old global-base behavior.)

### 4.2 Durability (source of truth)
- An **append-only durable log** is the source of truth. `remember` **flushes to disk BEFORE
  acknowledging** — no "stored" lies; a memory is durable before the API returns 200/201.
- A **corrupt durable/owners file is backed up** (`.corrupt.<ts>`) and the service **refuses to
  start** rather than silently wiping data.
- The backend flushes `owners.json` on `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT`.

### 4.3 Persisted embeddings (NEW)
- The **embedding vector is stored alongside the text** in the durable log, so a restart
  **rehydrates WITHOUT re-embedding the corpus** — boot cost is O(load), not O(embed all)). Legacy
  text-only entries embed once.

### 4.4 Worker-thread embedder (NEW)
- MiniLM runs in a **worker_thread** so embeds don't block the event loop.
- `EMBED_IN_PROCESS=1` forces in-process embedding; there is a transparent fallback to in-proc if
  the worker can't start.
title: StrongHold — System Documentation

text:
### 4.5 LucidLink — the fleet-wide single source of truth (the other headline)

The per-tenant COW memory above is the *semantic index*. **LucidLink is the canonical truth that
index points at.** It is not "one of the MCP tools" (that framing, in §12.1, is just the wiring) —
it is the architectural answer to the hardest problem in any multi-agent system: *where does shared
truth live when agents are ephemeral and spread across machines?*

LucidLink is a **planet-scale, streaming, mountable filesystem with one global namespace** (backed
by the owner's UGREEN MinIO object storage). That makes it the substrate that lets every agent —
regardless of which node or site it runs on — converge on the same canonical bytes:

- **One namespace, every node.** An agent on `spark-47d8`, another on `spark-a1d7`, the Mac, the
  Florida V0 fleet, or the California site all mount the *same* filespace and see the *same* files
  on demand. No replication, no sync conflicts, no "which copy is canonical" — the filesystem *is*
  the canon.
- **Truth outlives the agent.** Agents are ephemeral by design (`/fanout` spawns and `dismiss()`es
  them). Truth therefore cannot live in a context window or a per-node index; on LucidLink it lives
  in a durable, shared, **versioned** filesystem that no single agent owns.
- **Streaming, so memory isn't bounded by local disk.** A petabyte corpus, but each agent streams
  only the bytes it reads; hot data is cached locally, the long tail stays in object storage.
- **A coordination plane, not just storage.** Agent A writes a result; Agent B on another machine
  reads it. File-level semantics let agents coordinate *through the truth layer itself* rather than
  a fragile message bus.

**The fusion is the unique claim: a *metaharness whose shared source of truth is a planet-scale
filesystem*.** The COW vector/durable layer is the semantic index over that truth — agents recall
semantically, then read the authoritative bytes from LucidLink. The index can be rebuilt; the truth
never moves. No rented harness offers this, because (a) it has no incentive to let your agents
converge on *your* filesystem instead of its memory store, and (b) a metaharness over a sovereign
global filesystem is the opposite of the lock-in model.

> Current wiring (v0.1): the LucidLink MCP bridge is **read-only** (9 curated tools — see §12.1)
> and owner-scoped. The architecture above is the direction; read/write and per-tenant filespace
> scoping are the next steps toward agents treating LucidLink as a read-write shared workspace.

---
title: StrongHold — System Documentation

text:
## 5. Agents
Lightweight, addressable units that own a memory branch. Spawn → remember/recall → chat/act →
delete (graduate). Created via the API; backed by the ruflo agent registry.

---

## 6. Recall-augmented chat (`/chat`)
Single-shot chat that first recalls the agent's most relevant memories and injects them as context,
then answers via the model router. Supports **SSE token streaming** when `Accept:
text/event-stream` (local tier).

---

## 7. Agentic act loop (`/act`)
A real tool-using agent loop: **recall → inject memories → the model calls tools → results fed back
→ repeat (up to `maxSteps`) → concise final answer.** Returns a full `steps[]` trace. Built-in
tools:
- `run_code` — sandboxed code execution
- `recall_memory` — search the agent's memory
- `remember` — persist a fact
- plus any connected **MCP** tools (namespaced `server__tool`)

Works on any provider; for Claude the loop translates tool calls between OpenAI and Anthropic
formats automatically.

**Loop budget (security/resilience):** wall-clock `ACT_BUDGET_MS` (default 180000) plus a per-step
tool-call cap `MAX_TOOLCALLS_PER_STEP` (default 8).

---

## 8. Sub-agent fan-out (`/fanout`)
Spawn up to **8** ephemeral sub-agents, run tasks in parallel through the agent loop, aggregate
results, then **dismiss the workers (no graduation)**. Fan-out queues against the GPU semaphore so
it doesn't dogpile a single GPU; with the dual-GPU pool, two inferences run truly in parallel.
Fanout also takes per-task `{prompt, tools, profile}` for per-task tool selection.

---
title: StrongHold — System Documentation

text:
## 9. Sovereign code sandbox (`/sandbox/run` + the `run_code` tool)
Runs `python` / `node` / `bash` in an **ephemeral, locked-down Docker container** on your box:
- `--network none` (network-isolated)
- `--cap-drop ALL` (dropped capabilities)
- `--read-only` rootfs
- non-root user
- `/tmp` tmpfs **noexec**
- memory / CPU / pids / time limited
- auto-removed after the run

No code ever leaves your hardware. Toggle with `SANDBOX_ENABLED`. Public RCE is intentional but
strongly contained, behind JWT plus the global caps below. A **global sandbox container cap**
(`SANDBOX_MAX_CONCURRENCY`, default 4) bounds simultaneous containers.

---
title: StrongHold — System Documentation

text:
## 10. Model routing (`service/router.js`)

The caller **never names a model**; they pass an optional `tier`. The tier knob maps to an ordered
provider preference and fails over on error/timeout:

| `tier` | Provider order | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `fast` / `balanced` / `local` | `[local]` | Free, private, on your hardware |
| `auto` *(DEFAULT)* | `[local → cloud → openrouter]` | Local-first, cloud failover |
| `max` | `[cloud → openrouter → local]` | Best reasoning (Claude), then fallbacks |
| `openrouter` | `[openrouter → local]` | GPT/Gemini/Llama/… with local failover |

**Providers**
- **local** = Ollama, default model `qwen2.5-coder:32b` (served from the dual-GPU pool — see §11).
  The pool is **model-aware**: a bare model name still goes to local, routed to a pool host that
  actually has that model (see §10.1).
- **cloud** = Anthropic Claude `claude-opus-4-8`, used **only when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set**
  (otherwise the affected tiers resolve to local).
- **openrouter** = OpenAI-compatible endpoint (one key → GPT/Gemini/Llama/…), default slug
  `openai/gpt-4o`. An explicit `vendor/model` slug **prefers OpenRouter but keeps local as
  failover**.
- **compat** (NEW) = any **generic OpenAI-compatible** server you register — vLLM, `llama.cpp
  --server`, TGI, Open WebUI, LM Studio. Targeted by an explicit `<name>/<model>` slug; metered
  under the provider label `compat:<name>` (see §10.1).

**Behavior**
- **Graceful degradation**: a provider with no key is silently skipped — nothing breaks.
- **Per-provider failover** on error/timeout.
- The response **reports the `provider` + `model` that actually answered**.
- **Explicit model wins routing** — when a request names a model (a bare name, a `vendor/model`
  slug, or a `<name>/<model>` compat slug), routing follows what the model *is*, not the tier's
  default provider order (see §10.1).
- **Data egress**: `fast`/`balanced`/`local` stay 100% local; `max` and `auto`-fallback may use
  Claude; `openrouter`/slug uses OpenRouter; a `compat:<name>` slug goes to that registered server.
  Cloud is strictly opt-in per request.
title: StrongHold — System Documentation

text:
### 10.1 Multi-LLM routing beyond Ollama (NEW — config-driven)

StrongHold is no longer pinned to one local model + cloud. It routes to **any model on the cluster**
and **any OpenAI-compatible engine**, swappable purely by config with no code change. Two selection
modes operate on top of the tier knob; both are **backward compatible** — empty config = exactly the
prior behavior, and `providersFor` only routes by model when one is given, else the tier order is
unchanged.

**Model-aware Ollama pool.** Each request is routed to a pool host that actually **has** the
requested model, and the health gate **no longer requires the single default model**. So extra
models already loaded on the cluster Ollamas (e.g. `deepseek-r1:32b`, `qwen2.5:32b`, `llama3.1:70b`)
are reachable and metered **by name with zero config** — pass a bare model name and it goes to the
Ollama pool (never shadowed by another provider).

**Generic OpenAI-compatible provider** (`service/openai-compat.js`). A config registry of named
backends `{ name, url, apiKey?, models? }` for any OpenAI-compatible server — vLLM, `llama.cpp
--server`, TGI, Open WebUI, LM Studio. Config source (first found): env `LLM_BACKENDS` (inline JSON
array) → env `LLM_BACKENDS_CONFIG` (path) → `./llm-backends.json`. Target a backend with an explicit
**`<name>/<model>` slug** (e.g. `webui/llama3.1:70b`); usage is metered under provider label
`compat:<name>`. Real `llm-backends.json` is **gitignored** (holds API keys + private URLs); only
`llm-backends.json.example` is committed. Open WebUI needs a Bearer API key. `COMPAT_TIMEOUT_MS`
(default **120000**) bounds compat backend calls.

**Two selection modes.**
- **(a) Explicit model slug WINS routing** — route by what the model *is*, not the tier's default
  order. A bare model name → Ollama pool; a `vendor/model` slug → OpenRouter; a `<name>/<model>`
  slug → that compat backend.
- **(b) Tier→model aliases** (optional) — `TIER_MODELS` maps a bare tier to a specific cluster model
  so a tier resolves to a concrete model. Config source (first found): env `TIER_MODELS` (inline
  JSON) → env `TIER_MODELS_CONFIG` → `./tier-models.json`, e.g.
  `{"reason":"deepseek-r1:32b","big":"webui/llama3.1:70b"}`. Only `tier-models.json.example` is
  committed.

`routerInfo` (in `healthz.router`) now also reports **`compat`** (array of registered backend names,
or `false`) and **`tierModels`**.

**Activation:** `cp llm-backends.json.example llm-backends.json` (fill URL + key), optionally
`cp tier-models.json.example tier-models.json`, then restart the internal service
(`sudo systemctl restart agentmem-internal`). Extra Ollama models need no config.

---
title: StrongHold — System Documentation

text:
## 11. Dual-GPU load balancing (NEW — `service/ollama.js`)

Both DGX Sparks run Ollama; local inference is a **pool** load-balanced across them.

- `OLLAMA_URLS` (csv) lists the backends. Default:
  `http://spark-a1d7:11434,http://localhost:11434`. Legacy single `OLLAMA_URL` is still honored.
- Each backend gets a per-backend slot: `OLLAMA_CONCURRENCY` (default **1** = one GPU, one job) →
  **TRUE parallelism** (2 GPUs = 2 concurrent inferences). Verified: 2 concurrent requests ran on
  both GPUs at once; wall-time ≈ single, not 2×.
- The pool is **model-aware** (NEW): each request is routed to a backend that actually **has the
  requested model**, and the health gate **no longer requires the single default model** — so extra
  models already loaded on a cluster Ollama are reachable by name with zero config (see §10.1). A
  reachable backend is healthy; one still pulling the requested model is skipped for that request.
- On a call error, the request **fails over to the sibling backend before the router reaches
  cloud**.
- Background health re-check interval: `OLLAMA_HEALTH_MS` (default **15s**).

---
title: StrongHold — System Documentation

text:
## 11a. Observability — token/LLM usage metering (NEW)

Every model call's token usage is now **captured** from the provider (it was previously received
from upstream and discarded) and normalized to `{input, output, total}`. Ollama and OpenRouter read
the OpenAI `usage` block; cloud Claude reads `res.usage.{input_tokens, output_tokens}`. This makes
local (free/sovereign) vs. cloud (paid) spend — and per-model, per-backend cost attribution —
visible in real time, with no external dashboard.

- **Per call** — `chat`/`act`/`fanout` responses now include a `usage` block. `act` and `fanout`
  **sum** usage across every model call in the agentic loop (and across all sub-agents for fanout).
- **Cumulative** — the internal service `/healthz` now reports **`usageTotals` =
  `{ totals, byProvider, byModel }`**, each `{input, output, total, calls}`, since process start.
  `byModel` tracks each model by name (including `compat:<name>` backends).
- **Session** — the StrongHold MCP server keeps a per-session tally and exposes the new

  exponential backoff** (1s → 30s cap).

## 15. Auth & multi-tenancy (`backend/server.js`)

Bearer **JWT**, algorithm auto-detected:

- **Asymmetric Supabase (RS/ES/PS)** — verified against the **JWKS of the token's OWN issuer**

  asymmetric tokens are **REJECTED** unless `SUPABASE_ALLOW_ANY=1`.
- **JWKS serve-last-good (NEW):** if the IdP is briefly unreachable, the stale cached key is used

## 16. Security posture

| Control | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Fail-closed secrets (NEW)** | Both tiers refuse to boot on a default/weak/missing key: `API_KEY` on the internal service; `JWT_SECRET` and `INTERNAL_API_KEY` < 24 chars on the backend. |
| **Public auth** | Bearer JWT (asymmetric Supabase JWKS or HS256); `/health` is the only unauthed public route. |
| **Per-tenant isolation** | Caller only sees/uses/deletes their own agents; cross-tenant → 404. |
| **Internal auth** | Shared `X-API-Key`; internal service not exposed through the Funnel. |
| **Per-tenant rate limit (NEW)** | Token bucket: `RATE_BURST` 30 capacity, refill `RATE_PER_SEC` 1. Heavy ops (act/fanout/chat/sandbox) cost `HEAVY_COST` 5 → **429 + Retry-After**. |
| **Global heavy-op concurrency cap (NEW)** | `MAX_INFLIGHT_HEAVY` 4 simultaneous heavy jobs across all tenants → 429 when exceeded. |
| **Global sandbox container cap (NEW)** | `SANDBOX_MAX_CONCURRENCY` 4. |
| **Request body limit (NEW)** | `MAX_BODY_BYTES` 1,000,000 → **413**; malformed JSON → **400**. |
| **Per-request loop budget (NEW)** | `ACT_BUDGET_MS` 180000 wall-clock + `MAX_TOOLCALLS_PER_STEP` 8 per step. |
| **Sandbox** | Network-isolated, cap-dropped, non-root, read-only rootfs, `/tmp` noexec, resource-limited. Public RCE behind JWT + the limits above. |
| **Minimal MCP env (NEW)** | MCP children never receive the service secrets (see §12.3). |
| **Health info-leak closed (NEW)** | Unauthenticated `/healthz` returns only `{status, uptime}`; detailed diagnostics require the API key. |
| **CORS** | Enabled (`*` by default) so browser apps can call it; safe because auth is a Bearer token, not cookies. |
| **Secrets at rest** | Live ONLY on the host (`/etc/agentmem-internal.env`, `backend/.env`), never in git or the Docker image. The LucidLink `sa_live:` token lives only on ai-factory-mini in `~/.lucidlink/mcp-config.json`. |

- **Timeouts on every model call** so a hung host triggers failover, not a hang:

  `restart=unless-stopped`.

text:
## 18a. Economics (why the metaharness pays for itself)

StrongHold doesn't merely undercut a rented harness — it **inverts the cost curve**. A rented
harness is variable opex that rises with usage (the more value you extract, the more you pay,
indefinitely). StrongHold is sunk capex plus a near-zero marginal cost per request that *falls* per
unit as volume grows.

- **Marginal cost of a local call ≈ electricity, not a per-token fee.** The two DGX Sparks are
  already bought; once the capex is sunk, every additional local agent run is essentially free. The
  router defaults to the local pool, so the common path costs nothing per token.
- **The cost gap is widest exactly where the value is highest.** A one-shot chat is cheap to rent.
  An *agent* is not: `/act` issues up to `MAX_STEPS` (≤10) model calls per task (reason → tool →
  observe → repeat), and `/fanout` multiplies that by the number of sub-agents. A rented harness
  meters every one of those calls. Agentic workloads — the valuable ones — are precisely where
  renting hurts most and where owning the GPUs flips the math.
- **Cloud is opt-in and surgical.** Frontier token prices are paid *only* on `tier:max` (or an
  explicit `vendor/model` slug) requests that genuinely need Opus/GPT-class reasoning. The result
  is a **blended cost**: free local for the routine majority, premium cloud for the minority that
  earns it — versus paying a premium price for 100% of calls on a rented stack.
- **The memory layer is free.** Embeddings (`all-MiniLM-L6-v2`), vector storage, and recall all run
  on-device (§4.1). On a rented stack each is separately metered (per-embedding, per-vector stored,
  per-query). With LucidLink + the owner's MinIO (§4.5), one canonical copy streams to every agent —
  no charge to duplicate, sync, or query memory across machines or sites.
- **No replication tax across the fleet.** Because LucidLink is a single global namespace, adding a
  node or a site does not multiply storage or sync cost — agents stream the same canonical bytes.
  Object storage ($/TB) is far cheaper than a managed vector DB's per-vector/per-query pricing.
- **The metaharness is itself a cost-optimization engine.** Tiering routes cheap tasks to cheap
  models and spends frontier dollars only where they pay for themselves; swappability means no
  vendor can raise prices on us without us routing around them. **No lock-in = pricing power.**
- **It resells with structural margin.** Marginal cost per tenant is near zero, so a product built
  *on* StrongHold has gross margins bounded only by already-owned hardware. A competitor reselling a
  rented harness carries the vendor's per-token fee as a permanent floor under COGS.

**Net:** rent the frontier brain by the sip, for the 10% of calls that need it; own everything else.
Cost scales with hardware you control, not with a meter someone else runs.

## 25. Glossary
- **Harness** — everything around a model that lets it do work (loop, tools, sandbox, memory, auth,
  routing). Scoped to one vendor's model.
- **Metaharness** — a harness whose *models, tool runtimes, sandboxes, memory backends, and even
  other agent frameworks are interchangeable leaves*. It orchestrates harnesses; the model is a
  swappable commodity, not the center. StrongHold is a metaharness (§1a).
- **Single source of truth** — the one canonical store all agents converge on regardless of which
  node/site they run on. In StrongHold, LucidLink's global filesystem (§4.5); the COW vector memory
  is the semantic index over it.
- **Tenant** — an isolated memory owner, keyed by `<ref>:<sub>` (Supabase) or `hs:<sub>` (HS256).
- **Base / branch** — shared memory vs. a per-agent copy-on-write fork.
- **Graduate** — promote an agent's memories into the shared base on termination.
- **Tier** — the one-word quality/cost knob that selects a provider order.
- **Provider** — `local` (Ollama pool), `cloud` (Claude), `openrouter`, or `compat:<name>` (any
  registered OpenAI-compatible server — §10.1).
- **Profile** — a named tool bundle (`all`, `memory`, `code`, `files`, `research`, `lucid-readonly`).

*StrongHold is our Harness as a Service (HaaS).*

How to run, monitor, configure, and troubleshoot the system on `spark-47d8`.
Repo root: `/home/markt/agenticow-ruflo-memory`. Sudo: `markt` / password on file.

StrongHold is a sovereign, memory-centric AI-agent harness served as an API and
running entirely on our own hardware (two NVIDIA DGX Sparks). Two processes make

**Docker public backend** (`agentmem-backend`, :8771), fronted by a Tailscale

# durable log and reconnecting MCP servers (MCP boot is parallel).

# Public backend
cd /home/markt/agenticow-ruflo-memory/backend && docker compose up -d --build   # or: restart / down

text:
## 3. Dual-GPU Ollama pool

Both DGX Sparks run Ollama; local inference is a **pool** load-balanced across
them so two GPUs give true parallelism (2 concurrent inferences, wall-time ≈
single not 2×).

- `OLLAMA_URLS` (csv) lists the backends. Default:
  `http://spark-a1d7:11434,http://localhost:11434` (sibling GPU host + local 47d8).
- Each backend gets a per-backend slot `OLLAMA_CONCURRENCY` (default `1` = one
  GPU one job). Background health re-check every `OLLAMA_HEALTH_MS` (default
  `15s`). Legacy single `OLLAMA_URL` is still honored.
- A backend is **healthy only if reachable AND it has the model** — a host still
  pulling `qwen2.5-coder:32b` auto-excludes itself. On a call error the request
  fails over to the sibling backend BEFORE the router escalates to cloud.
- The pool is **model-aware**: extra models already loaded on a pool host
  (`deepseek-r1:32b`, `qwen2.5:32b`, `llama3.1:70b`) are reachable + metered by
  name with **no config** — see §15.

**Add a GPU host to the pool**
1. On the new host: install Ollama and `ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:32b`
   (`OLLAMA_MODEL`). The host stays excluded from the pool until the model is
   fully present.
2. Append its URL to `OLLAMA_URLS` in `/etc/agentmem-internal.env`, e.g.
   `...,http://new-gpu-host:11434`.
3. `sudo systemctl restart agentmem-internal`.
4. Verify in `/healthz`: `ollamaQueue.backends[]` and `ollama.backends[]` list
   the new url with `healthy:true`.

text:
## 4. LucidLink MCP bridge

Read-only access to LucidLink filespaces (9 tools: list_filespaces,
link_filespace, current_filespace, whoami, read_file, list_files, find_files,
grep_files, read_lines). The `lucidlink-mcp` package runs on **ai-factory-mini**
(spark is aarch64; the package has no ARM-Linux wheel) and is bridged to spark
over **SSH-stdio** (`command: ssh ... uvx lucidlink-mcp`), configured in
`mcp-servers.json`.

Operational requirements ON ai-factory-mini:
- `uv` / `uvx` must be installed (uvx launches `lucidlink-mcp`).
- The service-account token (`sa_live:…`) lives in
  `~/.lucidlink/mcp-config.json` ON THE MAC — never in git.

**CRITICAL GOTCHA:** the MCP server reads the token **once at startup**. The
persistent bridge must be (re)started **AFTER** the token file exists. If the
bridge was launched before the token was written, restart the internal service
(which respawns the MCP child) so it picks up the token:

```bash
sudo systemctl restart agentmem-internal
# then confirm the lucidlink server is ready (§5)
```
title: StrongHold — Operations Runbook

text:
### 4.1 Write bridge + per-tenant memory sync

A second bridge **`lucidlink-rw`** (read+write, confined to the `agenticow`
filespace = the `/stronghold-mem` common namespace) backs `mem-sync`. The
`stronghold-mem-sync.timer` (oneshot, `flock -n`, every 10 min, `User=stronghold`)
runs `service/mem-sync.mjs`, which mirrors COW memory + Claude markdown memory into
the namespace and, since 2026-06-30, writes a **per-tenant** export to
`tenants/<tenant>/memory.json` (that tenant's `tbase:<tenant>` graduated base + its
agents' private memories, grouped from the durable log via the tenant-tagged ruflo
agent store). The shared global base + Claude memory stay at the namespace root.

```bash
systemctl status stronghold-mem-sync.timer
journalctl -u stronghold-mem-sync.service -n 20   # "... ; tenants: N written, ..."
sudo -u stronghold .../node service/mem-sync.mjs --full   # force a complete re-sync
```

Inspecting the durable log: per-tenant graduated learnings live under scope
`tbase:<tenant>`; the global `base` scope holds only curated shared infra. A tenant
with no `tbase:*` scope and no tagged agents simply has no export folder yet.

### 4.2 Per-tenant filespace (hard isolation, ADR-0010)

For hard isolation, a tenant gets its **own** LucidLink filespace instead of an
`agenticow` subfolder. Provisioning is one idempotent script:

```bash
# creates filespace stronghold-<tenant>, a dedicated stronghold SSH key, the Mac
title: StrongHold — Operations Runbook

text:
# forced-command (running the confine-mcp.py shim), and the registry entry.
SUDO_PASS=… service/provision-tenant.sh <tenant>      # e.g. pilot01
sudo systemctl start stronghold-mem-sync.service       # push that tenant's memory
```

- **Confinement boundary** is `service/confine-mcp.py` (deployed to the Mac at
  `~/.lucidlink/confine-mcp.py`), run by the forced command instead of `lucidlink-mcp`
  directly. It strips `link_filespace`/`list_filespaces`, so the bridge key is pinned
  to the one filespace — LucidLink tokens are workspace-admin scope and cannot be
  narrowed, so this shim *is* the isolation. The `agenticow` rw bridge runs the same
  shim; the read-only bridge does not (it browses many filespaces by design).
- **Registry** `service/tenant-filespaces.json` maps `tenant → {filespace, key}`;
  `mem-sync` routes a registered tenant to its own filespace, unregistered ones to the
  subfolder fallback.
- **Verify a bridge is confined:** connect with the tenant key and call a file tool
  (e.g. `list_files /`) — it auto-links only `stronghold-<tenant>`; `link_filespace`
  to anything else returns "tool … is disabled on this filespace-confined bridge".
- **Deprovision (reverse order):** remove the tenant from the registry; drop the Mac
  `authorized_keys` line `lucidlink-rw-<tenant>`; delete the key
  `/home/stronghold/.ssh/id_ed25519_ll_<tenant>*`; `DELETE
  /api/v1/filespaces/<filespaceId>` (id is in the registry entry).

text:
## 5. MCP health & auto-respawn

MCP external tools (ruflo + lucidlink) are stdio children of the internal
service, namespaced `<server>__<tool>` and auto-added to the act loop.

- A dead MCP child (ssh bridge drop, ruflo crash) is detected and
  **auto-respawned with exponential backoff** (1s → 30s cap). `has()`/`call()`
  are gated on `ready`, and tools are read live so respawns restore them.
- MCP children get only a safe env allowlist (PATH/HOME/…) plus the per-server
  `env` override — never the service secrets.

**Read per-server health** from authed `/healthz` → `mcpServers[]`:

```bash
curl -s -H "x-api-key: <API_KEY>" localhost:8770/healthz | jq '.mcpServers, .degraded'
# each entry: { name, ready, tools, restarts, lastExit }
```

- `ready:false` with a climbing `restarts` and a non-zero `lastExit` = that
  server is flapping (check the bridge / package on its host).
- When any MCP server is down, top-level `status` goes `degraded` and
  `degraded.mcpDown[]` lists the offending server names. Auto-respawn keeps
  retrying; no manual action is needed unless a server stays down (then fix its
  host and it will reconnect, or restart the internal service).

## 6. Health checks

```bash
# Public (no auth) — {status, baseVectors, internal}
curl -s https://spark-47d8.tail333a1d.ts.net/agentmem/health
title: StrongHold — Operations Runbook

text:
# Internal full report (X-API-Key = internal API_KEY)
curl -s -H "x-api-key: <API_KEY>" localhost:8770/healthz
```

Unauthenticated `/healthz` returns only `{status, uptime}` (info-leak closed);
the detailed report requires the API key. Authed shape:

```
{ status: ok|degraded, uptime, degraded?:{mcpDown[]}, baseVectors, durableMemories,
  agents, rehydrated, sandbox, sandboxQueue:{active,queued,max},
  mcpServers:[{name,ready,tools,restarts,lastExit}], mcpTools,
  ollamaQueue:{queued,perBackend,backends:[{url,active,healthy}]},
  router, ollama:{reachable,backends[]}, ollamaUrl,
  usageTotals:{totals,byProvider,byModel} }
```

- `ollama.reachable` must be `true` for local/`fast`/`balanced` tiers.
- `router` reports which providers are live (cloud / openrouter `false` = no key);
  `router.compat` lists registered OpenAI-compatible backend names and
  `router.tierModels` the tier→model aliases (§15).
- `usageTotals` is cumulative token metering since boot — see §15.2.

## 9. Durability

- **Durable log is the source of truth** — an append-only log holds each memory
  with its text and its embedding vector. On restart the index rehydrates from
  the log WITHOUT re-embedding the corpus (boot cost O(load), not O(embed all));
  legacy text-only entries embed once.
- **Flush-before-ack** — `remember` flushes to disk BEFORE acknowledging, so a
  `200/201` never lies about a memory being stored. The backend also flushes
  `owners.json` on SIGTERM/SIGINT.
- **Corrupt-file refuse-to-start** — if the durable log or owners file is
  corrupt, the service backs it up as `.corrupt.<ts>` and **refuses to start**
  rather than silently wiping. Recovery: inspect/repair (or remove) the corrupt
  file, optionally restore from the `.corrupt.<ts>` backup, then restart.

```bash
title: StrongHold — Operations Runbook

text:
# After a refuse-to-start on corruption: locate the backup, then restart
ls -la /home/markt/agenticow-ruflo-memory/data/*.corrupt.*
sudo systemctl restart agentmem-internal
```

minting script **reads `JWT_SECRET` at runtime** (from `backend/.env` / env) and
must NEVER embed the secret value. Hand a colleague a token, not the secret.

```bash
cd /home/markt/agenticow-ruflo-memory/backend
# Script loads JWT_SECRET from the environment / .env at runtime — never hard-coded.
node scripts/mint-token.js --sub colleague-name        # prints a Bearer JWT
```

For real users, prefer asymmetric Supabase tokens (verified against the issuer's
JWKS; add the project ref to `SUPABASE_ALLOWED_REFS`).

## 11. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Local inference slow / `ollama.backends[].healthy:false` for a1d7 | spark-a1d7 down or tailnet offline | Pool **fails over** to localhost then router escalates to **cloud**; bring a1d7 back (`curl spark-a1d7:11434/api/tags`; see networking notes), it auto-rejoins once the model is present |
| `status:degraded`, `degraded.mcpDown[]` populated | An MCP child (ruflo / lucidlink ssh bridge) died | **Auto-respawn** is retrying (backoff 1s→30s). Fix the server's host if it stays down; lucidlink → confirm token file then restart internal service (§4) |
| LucidLink tools missing / unauthorized | Bridge started before token file existed (token read once at startup) | Ensure `~/.lucidlink/mcp-config.json` exists on ai-factory-mini, then `sudo systemctl restart agentmem-internal` |
| `429` + `Retry-After` | Per-tenant rate limit (`RATE_BURST` 30 / `RATE_PER_SEC` 1; heavy op costs `HEAVY_COST` 5) OR global cap (`MAX_INFLIGHT_HEAVY` 4) hit | Back off and retry per `Retry-After`; raise the limit knobs in `backend/.env` only if capacity allows |
| `413` request too large | Body exceeded `MAX_BODY_BYTES` (1,000,000) | Shrink the payload, or raise `MAX_BODY_BYTES` |
| Service refuses to boot, logs cite key | Fail-closed secrets: weak/missing `API_KEY` (internal) or `JWT_SECRET`/`INTERNAL_API_KEY` <24 chars (backend) | Set a strong (≥24 char) secret in the env file, restart |
| Service refuses to boot, cites corrupt file | Durable/owners file corrupt (backed up `.corrupt.<ts>`) | See §9 recovery |
| `tier:max` answers `provider:local` | No/invalid `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Check `/healthz` `router`; fix key + restart |
| Asymmetric token rejected | Project ref not in `SUPABASE_ALLOWED_REFS` (fail-closed) | Add ref to `SUPABASE_ALLOWED_REFS` (or set `SUPABASE_ALLOW_ANY=1`); `docker compose up -d` |
| Public calls 502 / hang | Internal service down | `systemctl status agentmem-internal`; restart |
| Leftover `agentmem-sbx-*` containers | Sandbox run interrupted | They live in **stronghold's rootless** daemon, not rootful: `sudo -u stronghold XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1001 DOCKER_HOST=unix:///run/user/1001/docker.sock docker ps -a --filter name=agentmem-sbx` then `docker rm -f`; normally auto-removed |
| Sandbox calls fail `spawn error` / `Cannot connect to the Docker daemon` | stronghold's rootless `docker.service` is down | `sudo -u stronghold XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1001 systemctl --user restart docker` (see §"Rootless sandbox") |

text:
## 12. Reboot behaviour

All layers are reboot-safe: `stronghold`'s **linger** is enabled so its user
manager + rootless `docker.service` come up at boot; systemd restarts the
internal service (`on-failure` + enabled) which rehydrates memory from the
durable log; Docker restarts the backend (`unless-stopped`); the Funnel config
persists. The internal service starts independently of the rootless daemon — the
sandbox is lazy (per-request), so a first sandbox call shortly after boot just
waits for the daemon to be ready. Verify with the two health checks in §6.
title: StrongHold — Operations Runbook

text:
## 13. Rootless sandbox (`stronghold` user)

The internal service runs as the dedicated unprivileged user **`stronghold`**
(uid 1001), which is **not** in the docker group, and executes sandboxed code on
its **own rootless Docker daemon**. This is the docker-privilege hardening: an
RCE in the harness process cannot reach the rootful socket or host root, and a
container escape maps to a `stronghold` subuid (powerless on the host).

**Layout**
- Service unit env: `User/Group=stronghold`, `DOCKER_HOST=unix:///run/user/1001/docker.sock`, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1001`, `HOME=/home/stronghold`, `UMask=0002`, plus pinned `REGISTRY_PATH`/`AGENT_STORE_PATH` (markt's `~/.claude-flow` state).
- Rootless daemon: user service `docker.service` under `stronghold` (image store under `/home/stronghold/.local/share/docker`). Sandbox images (`python:3.12-alpine`, `node:22-alpine`, `alpine:3.20`) are pre-pulled into it.
- App stays at `/home/markt/agenticow-ruflo-memory`; `stronghold` has it via **POSIX ACLs** (`getfacl` to inspect): rwX on the app dir + `~/.claude-flow/{swarm,agents}`, traverse on `/home/markt`. The LucidLink bridge uses `stronghold`'s **own** key + known_hosts under `/home/stronghold/.ssh/` (no ACLs on markt's `~/.ssh`).

**Manage the rootless daemon** (always set the two env vars):
```bash
S='sudo -u stronghold XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1001 DOCKER_HOST=unix:///run/user/1001/docker.sock'
$S systemctl --user status docker        # daemon state
$S systemctl --user restart docker       # restart it
$S docker ps -a --filter name=agentmem-sbx   # inspect sandbox containers
$S docker images                          # confirm the 3 images are present
$S docker pull python:3.12-alpine         # re-pull if an image is missing
```

**Verify isolation** (should all hold):
```bash
sudo -u stronghold docker -H unix:///var/run/docker.sock ps   # → permission denied (GOOD)
docker ps -a --filter name=agentmem-sbx                       # rootful: none (GOOD)
```

**If linger ever gets cleared** (rootless daemon won't start at boot):
`sudo loginctl enable-linger stronghold`.
title: StrongHold — Operations Runbook

## 15. Extra LLM backends & token-usage metering

StrongHold is no longer pinned to one local model + cloud: it routes to any model
already on the cluster Ollamas (§3) **and** any OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM,
llama.cpp `--server`, TGI, Open WebUI, LM Studio), swappable purely by config with
no code change. Every model call's token usage is now captured from the provider
and metered. **Empty config = exactly prior behavior** (backward compatible).
title: StrongHold — Operations Runbook

text:
### 15.1 Activate extra LLM backends

Extra **Ollama** models need **no config** — the pool is model-aware (each request
routes to a host that actually has the requested model, and the health gate no
longer demands the single `OLLAMA_MODEL`), so models already loaded on the cluster
Ollamas (`deepseek-r1:32b`, `qwen2.5:32b`, `llama3.1:70b`) are reachable + metered
by name. Target one with a bare model name (the Ollama pool is never shadowed).

For any **OpenAI-compatible** server, register a named backend:

```bash
cd /home/markt/agenticow-ruflo-memory
cp llm-backends.json.example llm-backends.json     # fill {name,url,apiKey?,models?}
cp tier-models.json.example tier-models.json       # OPTIONAL: tier→model aliases
# restart the internal service to pick up the new config (bang-shell sudo idiom):
printf '<pw>\n' | sudo -S -p '' systemctl restart agentmem-internal
```

- Each entry is `{ name, url, apiKey?, models? }`. **Open WebUI on `:8080` needs a
  Bearer `apiKey`.** Target a backend with an explicit model slug `"<name>/<model>"`
  (e.g. `"webui/llama3.1:70b"`) — an explicit slug **wins** routing (route by what
  the model IS, not the tier's default order). Usage is metered under provider label
  `compat:<name>`.
- `tier-models.json` maps a tier to a specific cluster model, e.g.
  `{"reason":"deepseek-r1:32b","big":"webui/llama3.1:70b"}`, so a bare `tier`
  resolves to that model.
- **Both files are gitignored** (they hold API keys + private URLs); only the
  `*.example` templates are committed — secrets stay on the host. Config can
  alternatively come from env: `LLM_BACKENDS` (inline JSON array) /
  `LLM_BACKENDS_CONFIG` (path), and `TIER_MODELS` (inline JSON) /
  `TIER_MODELS_CONFIG` (path); optional `COMPAT_TIMEOUT_MS` (default `120000`)
  bounds compat backend calls (§8).

### 15.2 Read token usage

```bash
title: StrongHold — Operations Runbook

text:
# Cumulative since boot — totals + per-provider + per-model
curl -s -H "x-api-key: <API_KEY>" localhost:8770/healthz | jq '.usageTotals'
```

- `usageTotals` = `{ totals, byProvider, byModel }`, each `{input, output, total,
  calls}`, since process start (each model/provider tracked by name; compat backends
  under `compat:<name>`). Makes local (free/sovereign) vs cloud (paid) spend visible
  in real time, with no external dashboard.
- **Per call:** chat/act/fanout responses now include a `usage` block; `act` and
  `fanout` SUM usage across every model call in the agentic loop / across all
  sub-agents.
- **Per session:** the `stronghold_usage` MCP tool (§14) returns this Claude Code
  session's per-session totals + per-tool breakdown (client-side; no backend call).

### 15.3 Verify a backend

```bash
# Confirm registered compat backends + tier aliases
curl -s -H "x-api-key: <API_KEY>" localhost:8770/healthz | jq '.router.compat, .router.tierModels'
```

- `router.compat` is an array of registered backend names (or `false` if none).
- **Compat backend:** an explicit-slug chat (e.g. model `"webui/llama3.1:70b"`)
  returns `provider: "compat:<name>"` plus a `usage` block — that pair confirms the
  backend is live and metered.
- **Extra Ollama models:** just call by name and confirm the model-aware route
  reaches a host that has it (usage then shows under that model in `byModel`).

### Notes

- The `stronghold_usage` tool ships in the MCP server code
  (`service/mcp-stronghold.js`), so it appears **only after a Claude Code session
  reload** (new MCP server code is loaded on respawn — §14).
- The **Docker public backend (:8771) needs no rebuild** — it proxies
  chat/act/fanout (and thus the new `usage` field) **verbatim**.

# StrongHold

*A sovereign Harness as a Service (HaaS).* A memory-centric AI agent harness — served as an
API, running entirely on your own hardware (two NVIDIA DGX Spark supercomputers). Per-user
persistent memory, recall-augmented chat, an agentic tool loop with a secure code sandbox,
external tools via MCP, sub-agent fan-out, and a model router (local-first, with optional
Claude / OpenRouter escalation) behind a one-word `tier` knob.

**Highlights**

- **Dual-GPU** — local inference is load-balanced across both DGX Sparks (true parallelism,
  automatic failover to the sibling GPU, then cloud).
- **LucidLink files** — agents can read & search the team's LucidLink filespaces (read-only,
  via an MCP bridge) using the `files` / `research` tool profile.
- **Per-task tool selection** — scope an agent's tools with one word (`profile`) or an explicit
  `tools` allowlist; enforced, not just advisory.
- **Token/LLM usage metering** — every model call's token usage is captured from the provider and
  normalized to `{input, output, total}`. `chat` / `act` / `fanout` return a per-call `usage` block
  (summed across the agentic loop and sub-agents); the internal `/healthz` reports cumulative
  `usageTotals` `{ totals, byProvider, byModel }`; and the MCP server exposes a `stronghold_usage`
  tool for per-session, per-tool totals — per-model and per-backend cost attribution, no external
  dashboard.
- **Config-driven multi-LLM routing** — no longer pinned to one local model + cloud. The Ollama pool
  is model-aware (extra cluster models like `deepseek-r1:32b` / `qwen2.5:32b` / `llama3.1:70b` are
  routable + metered by name with zero config), a generic OpenAI-compatible provider reaches any
  vLLM / llama.cpp / TGI / Open WebUI / LM Studio backend via an explicit `<name>/<model>` slug, and
  optional `tier`→model aliases map a one-word tier to a specific model — all swappable purely by
  config, backward-compatible (empty config = prior behavior).
- **Use it from Claude Code** — a zero-dep stdio MCP server (`service/mcp-stronghold.js`) exposes
  the whole harness as native tools to Claude Code / any MCP host (see `docs/DEVELOPER_QUICKSTART.md` §14).
- **Hardened & resilient** — runs as an unprivileged user on a rootless-Docker sandbox (a
  container escape ≠ host root), per-tenant rate limits, fail-closed auth, self-healing
  MCP/connection respawn, model-call timeouts + failover, and durable-before-ack memory.

# StrongHold — Roadmap

Where StrongHold is and what's next. StrongHold is **live, hardened, and multi-tenant
isolated** today; nothing below blocks internal use or a controlled pilot. This doc
tracks the path to broad multi-organization production and the improvements surfaced
along the way. Decisions live in [`docs/adr/`](docs/adr/README.md); this is the
forward view.

_Last updated: 2026-06-30._
title: StrongHold — Roadmap

text:
## Shipped (context)

- **Two-tier topology, dual-mode JWT auth, rootless-Docker privilege isolation,
  provider-agnostic model router, sovereign sandbox, MCP hub + tool profiles** —
  ADR-0001…0007, all live and verified.
- **LucidLink read+write, one common namespace** — agents read and write a single
  sovereign source of truth, no handoffs (ADR-0008).
- **Per-tenant memory isolation** — tenant-scoped graduation + recall; a tenant's
  learned knowledge never reaches another tenant (ADR-0009).
- **Per-tenant filespace hard isolation** — each provisioned tenant gets its own
  end-to-end-encrypted LucidLink filespace, bridge-confined by the `confine-mcp.py`
  shim so a tenant key cannot reach any other filespace; one-command provisioning;
  proven end-to-end with a reference tenant (ADR-0010).
- **Token/LLM usage metering + config-driven multi-model routing** — _DONE 2026-06-30
  (commit 68342fe)._ Every model call's token usage is captured and normalized
  `{input, output, total}`; `chat`/`act`/`fanout` return a per-call `usage` block,
  `/healthz` reports cumulative `usageTotals` `{ totals, byProvider, byModel }`, and the
  MCP server adds a `stronghold_usage` tool — per-model/per-backend cost attribution with
  no external dashboard. Routing is now config-driven: the Ollama pool is model-aware so
  extra cluster models (`deepseek-r1:32b`, `qwen2.5:32b`, `llama3.1:70b`) are routable +
  metered by name with zero config, plus a generic OpenAI-compatible provider and optional
  `tier`→model aliases — all backward-compatible (empty config = prior behavior). _Live in
  prod: metering + extra-Ollama-model routing. Coded but NOT yet activated: the extra
  non-Ollama backends (Open WebUI, vLLM) — they need API keys / private URLs in the
  gitignored `llm-backends.json` before use._

## Near-term — the multi-org gates

These are what stand between "pilot-ready" and "open multi-organization production."
title: StrongHold — Roadmap

text:
### 1. Cloud-spend caps + sign-up controls  ·  _priority: high_
Paid model tiers (Claude / OpenRouter) cost money per call, and any user from an
allowlisted Supabase project can authenticate. Per-tenant rate limiting and a global
heavy-op cap already bound abuse *rate*; what's missing is a hard *spend* ceiling and
tighter sign-up.
- Per-tenant monthly spend cap with a kill-switch when exceeded.
- Cost accounting per tenant (tokens × tier price), surfaced in health/admin.
  _(Token metering primitive shipped 2026-06-30 — `/healthz` `usageTotals` by
  provider/model; still TODO: per-tenant attribution × tier price + the spend cap itself.)_
- Keep `SUPABASE_ALLOWED_REFS` tight; sign-up gating before opening registration.
- _Ref: ARCHITECTURE_SECURITY risk #4._

### 2. Retire the prototype HS256 token  ·  _priority: medium_
A long-lived single-secret HS256 token bypasses the Supabase allowlist path. Rotate
`JWT_SECRET` and disable HS256 once all clients use Supabase asymmetric tokens.
- _Ref: ARCHITECTURE_SECURITY risk #5._

### 3. Self-service tenant provisioning UX  ·  _priority: medium_
`service/provision-tenant.sh` is fully scriptable today but operator-run. Wire it
behind the LucidLink workspace-manager gateway (or the product UI) so a tenant can be
provisioned (filespace + confined bridge + registry entry) without shell access, and
add a matching **deprovision** path (delete filespace, drop key + forced-command line,
remove registry entry) as a first-class, audited operation.

## Vendor-dependent — true token-level isolation

The biggest residual from ADR-0010: per-tenant filespaces give hard *cryptographic
data* separation, but the LucidLink **service-account token is workspace-admin scope**
and lives on the Mac, so a Mac compromise still exposes every filespace. The shim
confines the spark-side key holders; it does not shrink the token's own power. Two ways
to close this, both gated on a control-plane change:
title: StrongHold — Roadmap

text:
### 4. Per-tenant scoped tokens  ·  _depends on: LucidLink_
If LucidLink ships filespace-scoped service-account tokens (today every token is
workspace-admin), mint one per tenant and drop the shim's reliance — confinement would
move to the token itself. Track LucidLink's service-account roadmap.

### 5. Per-tenant LucidLink *workspace*  ·  _depends on: LucidLink account/billing_
A separate workspace per tenant gives each its own token that can only see that
workspace's filespaces — real token-level isolation without waiting for scoped tokens.
Creating workspaces is an account/billing operation outside the Service API we use for
filespaces; assess cost/automation before committing.

## Later / nice-to-have

- **Retroactive isolation** — ADR-0009 stops *new* cross-tenant leaks; pre-existing
  global-base content stays shared. A migration to re-scope or quarantine legacy
  global-base entries if a tenant needs a clean slate.
- **Per-tenant filespace lifecycle & billing visibility** — storage/cost per tenant
  filespace surfaced for capacity planning as tenant count grows.
- **mem-sync efficiency** — it opens the shared `agenticow` bridge even for a
  tenant-only sync (cheap, idempotent today; revisit at scale).
- **Genericized external doc variants** — customer-facing versions of the doc set.
- **Secrets manager** — move host env-file secrets behind a manager if the fleet grows
  (ARCHITECTURE_SECURITY risk #6).
